title: Why are some animals black and white?
speaker: BBC Learning English

sentences.en: Hello. This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是英国广播公司英文课的6分钟英语课

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Becca. Neil, what do the following animals have in common?
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔,我是贝卡 尼尔,下面的动物有什么共同点?

sentences.en: Zebras, giant pandas and magpies. That's pretty easy, Becca.
sentences.zh: 斑马 巨型熊猫和岩浆 很简单 贝卡

sentences.en: They're all black and white. Right! But do you know why these animals evolved to be black and white?
sentences.zh: 你知道这些动物为什么进化成黑白吗?

sentences.en: Hmm. I'm not so sure. Probably something about survival.
sentences.zh: 嗯,我不太确定 可能是关于生存的

sentences.en: That's usually the answer, isn't it? It is.
sentences.zh: 这通常是答案,不是吗?

sentences.en: The animal world is full of colour – shiny blue peacocks and bright green frogs.
sentences.zh: 动物世界充满了颜色 闪亮的蓝孔雀和明亮的青蛙

sentences.en: But in fact, hundreds of animal species are black and white.
sentences.zh: 但事实上 成百上千的动物是黑白种

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll try to find out why, while also learning some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 在这集中,我们会试着找出原因, 同时学习一些有用的新词和短语。

sentences.en: And remember, all the vocabulary from this episode is available on our website bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 记住,这集的所有词汇 都可以在网站bbclearingenglish.com上找到

sentences.en: OK. Time for a question for you, Becca. According to one theory, some animals are black and white to warn potential predators that they're dangerous or they taste bad.
sentences.zh: 好了 是时候问你了 Becca 根据一种理论 有些动物是黑白的 来警告潜在的掠食者

sentences.en: But what is the scientific term for this?
sentences.zh: 但科学术语是什么呢?

sentences.en: Is it: a) camouflage, b) mimicry, or c) aposematism?
sentences.zh: 是:a) 伪装,b) 模仿,或c) 隐蔽?

sentences.en: Well, Neil, I'm going to go with c) just because I've never heard of that word before.
sentences.zh: 尼尔,我要去C) 只是因为我从来没有听说过这个词。

sentences.en: OK. I like... I like your style! Some scientists think zebras' distinctive black-and-white stripes prevent bites from flies and other insects.
sentences.zh: 好,我喜欢你的风格,有些科学家认为斑马 独特的黑白条纹能防止苍蝇和其他昆虫咬人

sentences.en: Zoologist Dr Martin How tested this theory by covering horses, a close relative of the zebra, in stripes.
sentences.zh: 动物学家马丁博士 如何测试这个理论 通过覆盖马匹, 一个近亲斑马,条纹。

sentences.en: Here, Martin discusses his experiment with Caroline Steel from BBC World Service programme CrowdScience: Do we know what it is about the stripes that's putting them off?
sentences.zh: 这里,马丁讨论他与Caroline Steel的实验 来自英国广播公司世界服务节目Crowd Science:我们知道是什么 来拖住他们吗?

sentences.en: Is it somehow, like, visually confusing?
sentences.zh: 是不是有点像 视觉上的迷惑?

sentences.en: We originally set out to test whether maybe there were these optical illusions at play, so we did a whole bunch of tests where we tried different patterns of rugs, but it turned out that practically every high-contrast pattern, every black and white pattern we used, almost every pattern was really effective at stopping flies.
sentences.zh: 我们最初开始测试 是否有这些光学幻觉在玩耍, 所以我们做了一大堆测试 在那里我们尝试了不同的地毯模式, 但结果发现,几乎每一个高调模式, 每一个黑色和白色模式, 几乎每一种模式 都真正有效地阻止了苍蝇。

sentences.en: Martin conducted a whole bunch of – meaning a lot of – tests using different colours and patterns.
sentences.zh: 马丁用不同的颜色和模式 做了一大堆测试,这意味着很多。

sentences.en: Black and white stripes created an optical illusion, a visual trick that makes your eyes see things differently from how they really are.
sentences.zh: 黑白条纹创造了一种光学幻觉, 一种视觉把戏, 让你的眼睛看的东西 与它们的真实面貌不同。

sentences.en: As a result, the flies were put off. They lost interest and didn't bite.
sentences.zh: 结果,苍蝇被推迟了,他们失去兴趣,没有咬人。

sentences.en: So, zebras' stripes confuse insects, telling them to look elsewhere for food.
sentences.zh: 所以斑马的条纹混淆了昆虫 让他们去别处找食物

sentences.en: But are there other reasons animals are black and white?
sentences.zh: 但还有其它原因 动物是黑白的吗?

sentences.en: Nobody who's seen giant pandas in a zoo would find them hard to spot.
sentences.zh: 没有人在动物园见过巨型熊猫 会发现它们很难发现

sentences.en: Against a grassy background, they stand out easily.
sentences.zh: 在草根背景之下,它们很容易显露出来。

sentences.en: But seen from a distance in the snowy mountain forests where they live, black and white makes the perfect disguise.
sentences.zh: 但从雪山森林的远处看 黑白是完美的伪装

sentences.en: Here's Professor Tim Caro, a world authority on animal behaviour, explaining more to Caroline Steel for BBC World Service's CrowdScience: The giveaway for me was 15 photos of giant pandas, taken either fairly close up or at a distance, and in two of those photos, I was unable to see anything in the picture other than rocks and snow.
sentences.zh: 这是Tim Caro教授, 一家世界动物行为权威机构, 向Caroline Steel 解释英国广播公司世界服务社的《人群科学》: 对我而言, 15幅巨型熊猫的照片, 要么近距离拍摄, 要么远距离拍摄,

sentences.en: And then later on, I realised that in fact there was a giant panda in the centre of that picture some distance away.
sentences.zh: 之后,我意识到,事实上, 有一头巨型熊猫 在照片的中心某处很远的地方。

sentences.en: Immediately that... that clicked in my mind.
sentences.zh: 紧接着... 我脑海中闪烁着

sentences.en: The pandas were so well camouflaged Tim couldn't spot them in the photos.
sentences.zh: 熊猫伪装得很好 蒂姆在照片上看不到他们

sentences.en: That's when something clicked in his mind – a phrase used when you suddenly understand something after trying for a long time.
sentences.zh: 这就是他脑海中闪烁的东西-- 在你尝试了很长一段时间之后突然理解某事时使用的短语。

sentences.en: Tim understood that pandas use colour to hide.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆明白熊猫用颜色来隐藏

sentences.en: He calls this a giveaway – something that makes it easy for people to discover something secret or unknown.
sentences.zh: 他称这为“牺牲 ”, 让人们很容易发现一些秘密或未知的东西。

sentences.en: So, are animals black and white to repel insects, like zebras, or for camouflage, like pandas?
sentences.zh: 那么 黑白动物是用来击退昆虫 像斑马一样 还是用来伪装 像熊猫一样?

sentences.en: Let's give the final word to Hannah Rowland, a researcher into another black and white animal – penguins.
sentences.zh: 让我们给汉娜·罗兰最后一个字, 一个研究另一个黑白动物——企鹅的研究员。

sentences.en: Really, science never has a black-and-white answer – excuse the pun – about the... with penguins being black and white.
sentences.zh: 真的,科学从来没有一个黑人和白人的答案—— 原谅双关语—— 关于企鹅是黑人和白人。

sentences.en: It's often a very complex mixture of reasons.
sentences.zh: 这往往是非常复杂的混合原因。

sentences.en: The answer to why animals are black and white is not black and white – a situation described as black and white means one where it's easy to understand what's right and wrong.
sentences.zh: 为什么动物是黑白的, 答案不是黑白的, 一种被称为黑白的情况 意味着很容易理解什么是对的。

sentences.en: In fact, there's no one reason why animals are black and white.
sentences.zh: 事实上,没有任何理由 动物是黑白的。

sentences.en: Zebras avoid bites, pandas hide from predators and some animals, like skunks, warn other animals they're dangerous.
sentences.zh: 斑马避免咬人 熊猫躲在掠食动物面前 有些动物,如臭虫 警告其他动物它们很危险

sentences.en: It all depends on the specific animal. And talking of skunks reminds me of my question, Becca.
sentences.zh: 这都取决于具体动物 说到臭屁让我想起了我的问题 贝卡

sentences.en: According to one theory, some animals are black and white to warn potential predators they're dangerous or taste bad.
sentences.zh: 根据一种理论 有些动物是黑白的 来警告潜在的掠食者 它们很危险或者味道不好

sentences.en: But what is the scientific term? And I chose c) aposematism because I'd never heard of it before.
sentences.zh: 但科学术语是什么?我选择了(c) 套用,因为我从来没有听说过它。

sentences.en: Well, that's a great way of choosing. And it's done well for you because you're correct.
sentences.zh: 嗯,这是一个很好的选择方式 对你有好处,因为你是正确的

sentences.en: Woohoo! OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with optical illusion – a visual trick where your eyes perceive things differently from how they really are.
sentences.zh: 好吧,让我们回顾一下我们学到的词汇,从光学幻觉开始-- 一种视觉的把戏,你的眼睛对事物的感知与真实的感知不同。

sentences.en: A whole bunch of something means a lot of something.
sentences.zh: 一大堆的东西 意味着很多东西。

sentences.en: If something puts you off, it causes you to dislike it or lose interest.
sentences.zh: 如果有什么东西让你失望, 它让你不喜欢它或失去兴趣。

sentences.en: A giveaway is something that makes it easy for people to discover something secret or unknown.
sentences.zh: 放弃是使人们容易发现秘密或未知的东西。

sentences.en: The phrase something clicked in my mind is used when you suddenly understand something at last.
sentences.zh: 我脑海中被点击的词句 被使用 当你突然理解的东西 终于。

sentences.en: And finally, if you describe something as black and white, you mean it's easy to understand what is right and wrong.
sentences.zh: 最后,如果你把东西描述成黑白, 你的意思是很容易理解什么是对的,什么是错的。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, for a quiz and worksheet for this episode.
sentences.zh: 再一次,我们的六分钟已经到了, 但是去我们的网站,bbclearingenglish.com, 为这集的测验和工作单。

sentences.en: See you there soon. But for now, it's goodbye.
sentences.zh: 一会儿见,但现在再见了

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见!
